mgmt_bio.text: He is chairman of the board, chief executive officer and an executive director of Lenovo Group, having assumed the CEO role on 5 February 2009; he had previously served as chairman from 30 April 2005, and was CEO and an executive director from 16 December 1997. He joined Lenovo in 1989 and helped transform it into a global technology company serving customers in 180 markets, overseeing the acquisition of IBM's PC business in 2005 and of the IBM x86 server business and Motorola Mobility in 2014. In the 2025/26 annual report letter he reported record full-year results and emphasised Lenovo's leadership in hybrid artificial intelligence.

mgmt_recent.text: Lenovo named Diego Majdalani senior vice president and president for Latin America effective 12 October 2026, succeeding Sergio Buniac, who moved to Qualcomm as vice president and general manager in August 2026. Tareq Alangari joined in January 2026 as senior vice president and president for Middle East, Turkiye and Africa, while Sumir Bhatia became the first Asia Pacific chief commercial officer in April 2026 ahead of regional COO Ivan Cheung's June 2026 retirement. The board also disclosed a non-executive director resignation in April 2026 and an appointment in June 2026. Chairman and CEO Yang Yuanqing said Lenovo is becoming an "AI-native company," targeting $100 billion of annual revenue within two years via its hybrid AI strategy.

thesis_pillars.text: Lenovo Group Limited (HKSE: 992) delivered record first-quarter FY2026/27 revenue of US$26.9 billion, up 43% year-on-year, with all business groups at record first-fiscal-quarter revenue and operating profit, and adjusted profit up 176% to US$1.075 billion. Its hybrid-AI mix keeps rising, with AI-related revenue of US$9.3 billion, about 35% of total sales, after 105% AI revenue growth in FY2025/26. Infrastructure Solutions Group is scaling fast: revenue nearly doubled to US$8.5 billion at a 9.1% operating margin, with an AI server pipeline of US$54 billion, up 157% sequentially. Server share gains support this, as Lenovo took the worldwide lead in x86 server shipments in the second quarter of 2026, with volumes up 45.6%.
